Title: Verify successful login with valid standard_user credentials
Precondition: The login page at https://www.saucedemo.com/ is reachable in staging. The account 'standard_user' with password 'secret_sauce' is active and not locked.
Steps: 1. Navigate to https://www.saucedemo.com/ → Expected: The login form is displayed with a 'Username' field, a 'Password' field, and a 'Login' button | 2. Enter 'standard_user' into the field with placeholder 'Username' → Expected: The Username field shows the value 'standard_user' and no validation error is displayed | 3. Enter 'secret_sauce' into the field with placeholder 'Password' → Expected: The Password field renders the input as masked dots and no validation error is displayed | 4. Click the 'Login' button → Expected: The visitor is authenticated and redirected to the inventory page at https://www.saucedemo.com/inventory.html
Expected Result: The visitor is authenticated and taken into the application (inventory page). No error banner is shown.

Title: Verify repeated failed login attempts do not lock or throttle the account (characterization)
Precondition: The login page at https://www.saucedemo.com/ is reachable. The account 'standard_user' exists with password 'secret_sauce'.
Steps: 1. Navigate to https://www.saucedemo.com/ → Expected: The login form is displayed | 2. Enter 'standard_user' with an incorrect password and click 'Login', repeating this 10 times in succession → Expected: Each attempt returns the standard bad-credentials error banner | 3. Observe whether any attempt is blocked, delayed, or returns a lockout/throttle message → Expected: Record whether the system throttles, locks out, or continues accepting attempts | 4. On the 11th attempt, enter 'standard_user' with the correct password 'secret_sauce' and click 'Login' → Expected: Document the result; if no lockout is implemented, the correct credentials authenticate successfully and this behavior is recorded as absent-by-design
Expected Result: The throttling/lockout behavior is characterized and documented, either as enforced or explicitly absent-by-design.
